summary.suggested: The Daily Missouri Democrat reported claims that the Mace-Coburn fight was fixed. Interviewed at his Washington Avenue saloon after returning, Tom Allen, Mace's second, said he did not believe it and blamed Mace's broken hand.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads 'Daily Democrat', Tuesday morning, December 5, 1871. Before the 1875 merger, so not the Globe-Democrat.

facts.fact: Allen returned to St. Louis from the Mace-Coburn fight, the day before he was interviewed at his Washington Avenue saloon
places: Tom Allen's saloon, Washington Avenue, St. Louis
facts.quote: Returned yesterday. Didn't stay long after it was over.

facts.fact: Allen said Mace would have beaten Coburn had he not broken his hand early in the fight
facts.quote: Well, if Mace hadn't broke his hand in the first round, he'd made short work of "the Roman." After that he had to be on the defensive.

facts.fact: Allen denied the Mace-Coburn fight was fixed, saying he had more money on Mace than backer Al Smith
facts.quote: I don't believe it. Al Smith thinks so? Well, I had more money on Mace than he. I don't think Mace would throw his backers so.

facts.fact: Allen said he claimed a foul for Mace at the fight but the referee would not listen, and a man pulled a revolver on him
facts.quote: One fellow pulled a revolver on me, and told me to shut up, that I had nothing to say about it.

facts.fact: Allen said Coburn was the better man towards the end of the fight, as Mace was nearly gone from the cold
facts.quote: Coburn, and if he had followed Mace a half hour longer he would have won even without striking a blow, for Mace was nearly gone from cold.

notes: Interview took place 'yesterday afternoon' (Dec. 4); Allen's 'returned yesterday' would put his return about Dec. 3. Allen says Mace broke his hand in the first round; the fight reports say the second. Focus raised to primary since half the article is Allen's interview and the headline names him.
